Read the plan at `/Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmerMANN-skills/.runs/SFCC-83+84/plan.md` first — specifically step B1 ("ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid organism + recipe"), which has extensive, already-researched detail: exact Figma node citations, exact confirmed spacing values, exact confirmed typography, and a confirmation that the card variation/hover-behaviour question is already fully answered (no new `ZimmProductCard` work needed).

Also read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/` (`index.tsx` and `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`) in full — the sibling rail organism (SFCC-83's own, already built and tested), which is your closest structural precedent: same recipe-registration pattern, same named-constant-with-pending-promotion-comment style for un-tokenised-but-confirmed spacing values, same test/story conventions. This grid organism should follow the identical patterns, adapted to a 4-up grid instead of a horizontal scroller.

**One thing already fixed today that directly applies here — read it before writing your own title/count styling:** `zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx`'s `title` prop just had a real bug fixed (found via live Storybook testing): the title was rendering in the wrong font weight because no `textStyle` was applied. The fix applies `textStyle="heading3"` directly where the title renders. **Your title/item-count bar needs the exact same `heading3` textStyle** — the plan's B1 section independently confirms this same token via a completely different source (Figma `get_variable_defs` on the Full History page's own title bar, cross-checked against `typography.ts`) — so this isn't a guess, it's confirmed twice over. Apply `textStyle="heading3"` to both the title text and the item-count text from the start; don't repeat the mistake of leaving it unstyled and deferring to a caller.

**Create** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedGrid/` — `index.tsx`, `zimmRecentlyViewedGrid.css.ts`, `index.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`. Register `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid` in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts` (check how `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` is registered there and follow the identical pattern).

Props: `title: ReactNode`, `itemCountLabel: ReactNode` (a pre-formatted, already-pluralized string/node — e.g. "16 Items" — built by the caller using proper ICU plural handling; this component does not own copy/intl, same discipline as the rail), `cards: readonly ZimmProductCardProps[]`. Cards render at `variation: 'plp'` (already-shipped, already-tested variation — badge on, hover-swap on, size chips on — nothing new needed on `ZimmProductCard` itself for this).

Layout: title left / item-count right in a header row (`textStyle="heading3"` on both, per above), above a 4-up desktop grid. Confirmed spacing from the plan: vertical gap between rows is 64px and **does** have a real registered token (`--zimm-scale-1600` — check `zimmTokens.ts` to confirm the exact CSS var name) — use the real token, not a named constant. Horizontal gap between the 4 cards is 96px and does **not** have any registered token (checked exhaustively against zimmTokens.ts's full numeric scale) — use a named constant with an inline comment stating it's a confirmed Figma value pending foundation-scale promotion, exactly matching the pattern `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`'s own `CARD_WIDTH_MOBILE`/`TABLET`/`DESKTOP` constants already establish (read that file's comments for the exact wording style to match). Card size is 288x542 at desktop. Tablet/mobile column counts: the plan says derive from `grid.columns` (`base: 4, md: 8, xl: 10`) rather than inventing — read `overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts` (or wherever `grid.columns` actually lives — confirm the import path) to get the real values, and if a specific tablet/mobile column-count-for-this-grid can't be cleanly derived from those, leave it inherited/simple (e.g. 2-up mobile, matching the general responsive halving pattern already used elsewhere in this codebase) and comment why, per this codebase's "don't guess design values" rule — do not invent a specific pixel-perfect mobile/tablet layout with no source.

Pass criteria from the plan, verify each: recipe key namespaced `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid` (not reusing any base SFCC recipe name); `recipeGuards.test.ts` and `ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts` both still pass after your registration; explicit media queries off `breakpoints` from `app/theme/foundation`, never Chakra's array shorthand (the rail's own `.css.ts` shows the exact pattern — copy it); order of `cards` preserved verbatim (test with a distinguishable, non-alphabetical ordering, and make the test fail first by reversing before fixing, matching the rail's own already-proven test pattern for the identical concern); item count text comes from the `itemCountLabel` prop directly, not recomputed from `cards.length` internally (that computation belongs to the caller, per the props above — but DO add a story/test proving the two stay in sync when a real caller wires them together correctly, so a future divergence between the display count and the actual rendered count is at least visible in the story even though this component itself just trusts the prop). Story titled `Commerce/ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid` per `.claude/rules/components.md`'s categorisation table; named exports `Default`, `SingleItem`, `ManyItems`. Header comment in every new file noting this design is confirmed (not provisional — unlike B1's original plan text which called the source provisional before this session's own Figma verification pass confirmed the real values directly; read the plan's own B1 section for the exact citation to use).

After: run `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npm run audit:tokens` (must show no new finding under this new folder), and this component's own test suite. **Verify visually against the real running Storybook instance** — it should already be running; do not start it. If you have a way to reach it (check what port it's on — try `http://localhost:6006`, the Storybook default, or check `package.json`'s storybook script for the real port), use `npx test-storybook` scoped to this new story if that's set up in this repo, or at minimum confirm the story file itself builds without error via Storybook's own build/check mechanism. If you cannot actually reach a running Storybook instance, say so plainly rather than assuming success.

If you hit genuine ambiguity, decide from existing codebase precedent (the sibling rail organism is your primary precedent throughout) and list the decision with reasoning in your final report — do not stop and ask, do not leave a TODO.

Do not modify `zimmRecentlyViewedRail/*` itself (read-only precedent, not something to change) or any other existing file except the one registration line in `theme/components/index.ts`. Do not run `git commit`. Report back: what you built, the exact tablet/mobile column-count decision and why, tsc/test/audit-tokens results, the Storybook verification result, and your list of autonomous decisions.

37	
38	### Architecture fork — resolved: override `recommended-products/`, which removes the Cart port
39	
40	Verified directly at `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`.
41	`isFromExtends` returns true when the request names `@salesforce/retail-react-app` **and the issuing
42	file is not itself inside `overrides/`**. The plugin's own comment (lines 116–127): *"This will return
43	true if the issuer is a file in a base template... This allow the base template to import from
44	overrides."* Implementation: `this.extends.includes(pkgName) && !filepath.includes(issuerPath)`.
45	
46	Base Cart imports at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36`:
47	`import RecommendedProducts from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products'`
48	— a package-path import issued from a base file, so it **is** redirected once our override exists.
49	Base Cart is itself loaded by base `routes.jsx` via a relative `import('./pages/cart')`, which is not
50	redirected — so base Cart keeps rendering and picks up our override for free.
51	
52	**Consequence: the ~2,460-line Cart copy-first (`index.jsx` 1515 + 8 real partials ≈ 948) is not
53	required.** This departed from adjudication item #10 ("we only have to copy-first for cart"), in the
54	direction of *less* work. **APPROVED by Marcel, 2026-09-06**, on the evidence that this is already the
55	dominant pattern in this repo: nine component overrides shadow base paths and are reached purely by
56	the resolver (`icons` at 64 base import sites — and mandated by AGENTS.md — `responsive` 12,
57	`product-view` 6, `drawer-menu`/`list-menu` 2 each, `header`/`footer` 1 each). The single page port
58	(`product-detail`) exists only because base `routes.jsx` loads pages by *relative* import, which the
59	resolver never redirects — a constraint that does not apply to components. Open Question 5 is closed.
60	
61	**Caveat:** this is a *build-time webpack* resolver. It runs in the dev server and production build
62	only — **not** Storybook (`.storybook/main.js` aliases straight to `node_modules`) and **not** Vitest.
63	So the Cart behaviour cannot be proven by any automated test in this repo; it must be checked in the
64	running app. That is why A1's pause is a hard gate.
65	
66	Cost of this choice: the override module loads at **four base import sites serving eight rails**, not
67	five as an earlier draft of this plan stated:
68	
69	| Base import site | Rails | Takes the new branch? |
70	|---|---|---|
71	| `app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36` | Cart Recently Viewed, Cart May-Also-Like | **Yes** (1 of 2) |
72	| `app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx:40` | *(shadowed by our own PDP override — 3 rails)* | **Yes** (1 of 3) |

78	`CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED`, `constants.js:156,160`). **Two rails take the new branch; the other six must

82	`overrides-plugin.js`'s actual source, not just this plan's earlier paraphrase of it.** The
83	table's "Yes (1 of 3)" for `product-detail/index.jsx:40` describes the **base** file's import —

216	**The seam, precisely — this is what makes the later swap small.** Two independent concerns, today

218	1. **"Which product IDs has this shopper recently viewed?"** — today: read from browser storage,

221	2. **"Given those IDs, fetch real product data and turn it into cards"** — a live Shopper Products

243	- **B2** — same swap: the page container calls the new history hook instead of
244	  `getRecommendations`, and feeds the stored ID list (**capped at 24, not the rail's 5-item

248

250	- **Guests:** `sessionStorage` — unchanged from A4's existing design, still correctly satisfies AC 6

252	- **Registered shoppers:** `localStorage` — a genuine, explicit, temporary deviation from both AC 7
253	  ("available on login from any device") and the ticket's own Assumption ("storage... handled by
254	  SFCC"). `localStorage` survives closing the browser (better than nothing, testable), but is still
255	  **device-local** — it cannot and will not satisfy cross-device continuity. This is not a
256	  workaround for that AC, it's an explicit, stated non-fix pending the Einstein follow-up — must be
257	  called out plainly in the PR body and to whoever signs off testing, not discovered by a confused
258	  reviewer. AC 7 should be marked N/A-pending-follow-up for this PR, not silently tested against a
259	  single device and called passing.
260	- **De-duplication / ordering:** viewing a product already in history moves it to the front rather

557	Einstein history even on a fresh device. **That assumption breaks entirely once Einstein is out of
558	the loop** — there is no server-side history to trust anymore. Built as originally specced, every
559	registered shopper would show `hasRecentlyViewed = true` unconditionally, including one who has
560	never viewed anything in this interim system on any device — gating the rail *open* with zero real
561	cards behind it. That's a real, shippable bug, not a hypothetical; it must not be carried into the
562	interim build. **Corrected logic:**
563	
564	```
565	hasRecentlyViewed = recentlyViewedIds.length > 0
566	```
567	
568	— true for both guests and registered shoppers alike, based purely on this interim system's own
569	tracked history. `isRegistered` still matters, just for a different purpose now: it selects *which*
570	storage to read/write (see below), not whether to bypass the check.
571	
572	**New return shape:** `{hasRecentlyViewed: boolean, recentlyViewedIds: readonly string[],
573	markProductViewed: (productId: string) => void}` — the boolean is now derived from the ID list, not
574	tracked independently, so the two can never disagree.
575	
576	- `markProductViewed(productId)` writes to `sessionStorage` (guest) or `localStorage` (registered,
577	  via `isRegistered` from `useCustomerType()` — the same hook `use-einstein.js:449` already uses) —
578	  called from the existing Einstein `useEffect` in
579	  `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (lines 772–801), alongside the
580	  `einstein.sendViewProduct` calls already there (left untouched — that call is unrelated real
581	  analytics, not this build's concern). One import, one call, guarded by the same `if (product)`.
582	- **De-duplication / move-to-front:** if `productId` is already in the stored list, remove the old
583	  entry before prepending — never a duplicate, and a re-view correctly becomes "most recent" again.
584	- **Cap the stored list** at `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` (**24, superseded from an earlier
585	  500 same day — see §2** — matches the Full History page's own 24-ID fetch cap, since nothing
586	  beyond item 24 is ever displayable) — trim from the tail, oldest-first, on write.
587	
588	**AC mapping, restated for the interim system:** `sessionStorage` is session-scoped and cleared at
589	session end — **AC 6**, unchanged. **AC 7 (cross-device for registered shoppers) is explicitly
590	*not* satisfied by this interim design** — `localStorage` is still device-local. This must be stated
591	plainly in the PR body and marked N/A-pending-the-Einstein-follow-up for this specific AC, not tested
592	against a single device and reported as passing. See §2's "Interim data source" for the full
593	reasoning — this is a stated, accepted gap, not an oversight.
594	
595	**Confirmed 2026-09-07, not a frontend gap** (pre-dates and is unaffected by this revision — restated
596	for continuity): SFCC-83's own Assumptions section states *"the storage of Recently Viewed is
597	handled by SFCC."* The interim system above is a **temporary, explicit stand-in** for that
598	assumption while Einstein is unavailable, not a rejection of it — once the Einstein follow-up lands,
599	this hook's job reverts to a thin boolean/gate again and the real history moves back server-side, per
600	the original design intent this section used to describe.
601	
602	**Superseded by the above, not applicable to the interim build:** the old "stated assumption" about
603	a registered shopper with genuinely zero Einstein history still seeing a two-product baseline
604	(Open Question 6's original framing) — that residual was specific to trusting Einstein's own
605	baseline behaviour, which the interim system never calls, so it cannot leak through here. It returns
606	once the Einstein follow-up is built, at which point Open Question 6's original text applies again.
607	
608	**Pass criteria**
609	- SSR-safe: initial state `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: []}`, resolved in
610	  `useEffect`. No storage access during render. No hydration mismatch — the rail does not exist on
611	  first paint and appears after hydration. (Also good for LCP; the PDP rail is inside
612	  `<Island hydrateOn='visible'>` anyway.)
613	- Wrapped in `try/catch` — Safari private mode throws on both `sessionStorage` and `localStorage`.
614	  Failure degrades to `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: []}`, never an exception.
615	- JSDoc with `@returns` (`components.md` > Hooks).
616	- Vitest: empty storage + guest → `false`/`[]`; one ID + guest → `true`/`[id]`; empty storage +
617	  **registered** → `false`/`[]` (**the corrected case — must be tested explicitly, since this is
618	  exactly where the old short-circuit bug would have shipped silently**); re-viewing an existing ID
619	  moves it to front with no duplicate; writing past the cap trims the oldest entry; storage throwing
620	  → safe empty default; first render before effect → safe empty default.
621	- **Make each fail on purpose first.** The FED handbook's finding 18 trap is a test that passes
622	  because it was written against the only arrangement already correct — this applies doubly to the
623	  registered-with-zero-history case above, since that's precisely the case the old logic got wrong.
624	- The PDP change is exactly two lines (now passing `product.id` into `markProductViewed`, not a
625	  no-arg call). Nothing else in `product-detail/index.tsx` moves (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #5 — no
626	  refactoring upward).
627	
628	### A5 — `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` organism + recipe
629	
630	Create `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/` (`index.tsx`,
631	`zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`, `index.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`); register
632	`ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.
633	
634	**Purely presentational — data as props.** Props: `title: ReactNode`, `cards: readonly
635	ZimmProductCardProps[]`, `seeAllHref?: string`, `seeAllLabel?: string`. No `useEinstein`, no
636	`useIntl` — the container owns the copy. (An `IntlProvider` wrapper is still needed in the test
637	because `ZimmProductCard` itself calls `useIntl`; follow `zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx`'s wrapper.)
638	
639	Structure mirrors Figma: a `title-and-link` row (title left, See-Full-History link right) above a
640	horizontally scrollable `group` of `ZimmProductCard`s at `variation: 'recentlyViewed'`.
641	
642	**No rail-level arrow buttons.** Desktop `40000307:12444` decomposes into exactly two children —
643	`title-and-link` (1440×96) and `group` (1440×432) — with no arrow layer. `ZimmProductCard` already
644	carries its own intra-card arrows; rail arrows would collide. Native scroll with scroll-snap only.
645	
646	**Three explicit media queries** off `breakpoints` imported from `app/theme/foundation`, never Chakra's
647	array shorthand (it fails `recipeGuards.test.ts`). Real geometry, read from the nodes 2026-09-06:
648	
649	| Viewport | Rail node | Card | Cards across |
650	|---|---|---|---|
651	| Mobile (base, 402) | `40000538:25030` — 402×355.82 | **201×299.82** | **2** (201×2 = 402, exactly full-bleed) |
652	| Tablet (`breakpoints.md`, 768) | `40000730:13363` — 768×437.85 | **256×381.85** | **3** |
653	| Desktop (`breakpoints.xl`) | `40000307:12444` — 1440×528 | **288×432** | **5** |
654	
655	All three cards are 2:3, matching `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s existing `aspectRatio: '2 / 3'` — so card
656	width is the only thing that varies per breakpoint; height follows. Header (`title-and-link`) is
657	**h96** on Desktop (`40000538:20306`) and **h56** on Mobile (`40000538:25031`); the link is present on
658	both, so it is never hidden by viewport.

# SFCC-83 + SFCC-84 — Build Plan

**Produced:** 2026-09-06 · **Gate:** `findings.md` (four passes, cleared at the 2026-09-06 adjudication)
**Base branch:** `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component` (PR #85, open, unmerged)

## 1. Goal statement

Build the Recently Viewed rail and its full-history page per **SFCC-83** and **SFCC-84** (ACs in Jira
`customfield_10231`), designed in **`Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` component set `40000587:38471`**
(Desktop `40000307:12444`, Tablet `40000730:13363`, Mobile `40000538:25030` — all authoritative,
corroborated by PDP-template instances `7998:13508` / `8272:28947`), with SFCC-84's page from the
**provisional** `Zimmermann_Designs` `3332:35655` — following `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`
(token hierarchy) and `.claude/rules/components.md` (container/presentational split), and extending
**PR #85 / SFCC-236's** `ZimmProductCard` family via a **new `VARIATION_CONFIG` entry** (not a new
card), a **copy-first override of `recommended-products/`**, and **co-located `<name>.css.ts`**
recipes registered in `theme/components/index.ts`.

**Scope corrected 2026-09-07 against the real Jira AC text** (Marcel supplied the full verbatim
SFCC-83/SFCC-84 tickets; see "PLP surface" in §2 and the Open Questions for the full reconciliation).
This plan's original scope line — "follows `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4 (PDP + Cart); PLP is out;
SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly not met" — was written against the PRD, never checked against the ticket's
own AC text, and is **superseded, not merely refined**: the AC states plainly *"Confirmed surfaces
are PLP, PDP, and Cart."* PLP is real, in-scope, unbuilt work — see §2.
**No consent gating** — not a development-phase carve-out awaiting a later fix, but genuinely out of
this ticket's scope: Jasmijn's own dependency note ("move the consent acceptance criteria to a
separate user story") and comment history move consent ACs to SFCC-106. Must still be stated in both
PR bodies so a reviewer doesn't read the absence as an oversight.

**🔴 Data source corrected 2026-09-08 — Einstein is confirmed "Not Deployed" on every real
Zimmermann site (Open Question 6).** By Marcel's explicit direction, this build ships against real,
live Commerce Cloud product data sourced by this browser's own tracked view history instead — see
§2's "Interim data source" for the full design. A follow-up ticket (not yet created, Open
Question 18) swaps in real Einstein later; this plan's A3/A4/A6/B2 steps are written against the
interim design already.

## 2. Scale call

### Architecture fork — resolved: override `recommended-products/`, which removes the Cart port

Verified directly at `node_modules/@salesforce/pwa-kit-dev/configs/webpack/overrides-plugin.js`.
`isFromExtends` returns true when the request names `@salesforce/retail-react-app` **and the issuing
file is not itself inside `overrides/`**. The plugin's own comment (lines 116–127): *"This will return
true if the issuer is a file in a base template... This allow the base template to import from
overrides."* Implementation: `this.extends.includes(pkgName) && !filepath.includes(issuerPath)`.

Base Cart imports at `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36`:
`import RecommendedProducts from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/recommended-products'`
— a package-path import issued from a base file, so it **is** redirected once our override exists.
Base Cart is itself loaded by base `routes.jsx` via a relative `import('./pages/cart')`, which is not
redirected — so base Cart keeps rendering and picks up our override for free.

**Consequence: the ~2,460-line Cart copy-first (`index.jsx` 1515 + 8 real partials ≈ 948) is not
required.** This departed from adjudication item #10 ("we only have to copy-first for cart"), in the
direction of *less* work. **APPROVED by Marcel, 2026-09-06**, on the evidence that this is already the
dominant pattern in this repo: nine component overrides shadow base paths and are reached purely by
the resolver (`icons` at 64 base import sites — and mandated by AGENTS.md — `responsive` 12,
`product-view` 6, `drawer-menu`/`list-menu` 2 each, `header`/`footer` 1 each). The single page port
(`product-detail`) exists only because base `routes.jsx` loads pages by *relative* import, which the
resolver never redirects — a constraint that does not apply to components. Open Question 5 is closed.

**Caveat:** this is a *build-time webpack* resolver. It runs in the dev server and production build
only — **not** Storybook (`.storybook/main.js` aliases straight to `node_modules`) and **not** Vitest.
So the Cart behaviour cannot be proven by any automated test in this repo; it must be checked in the
running app. That is why A1's pause is a hard gate.

Cost of this choice: the override module loads at **four base import sites serving eight rails**, not
five as an earlier draft of this plan stated:

| Base import site | Rails | Takes the new branch? |
|---|---|---|
| `app/pages/cart/index.jsx:36` | Cart Recently Viewed, Cart May-Also-Like | **Yes** (1 of 2) |
| `app/pages/product-detail/index.jsx:40` | *(shadowed by our own PDP override — 3 rails)* | **Yes** (1 of 3) |
| `app/hooks/use-add-to-cart-modal.js:30` | add-to-cart modal (`pdp-similar-items`) | No |
| `app/pages/product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx:20` | PLP empty-search top-sellers, most-viewed | No |

It is therefore a **faithful port plus exactly one branch**, keyed off
`EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` (`'viewed-recently-einstein'` — the same string as
`CART_RECENTLY_VIEWED`, `constants.js:156,160`). **Two rails take the new branch; the other six must
render identically before and after** — a hard pass criterion.

**🔴 Correction, 2026-09-06 — the PDP row above is misleading, verified directly against
`overrides-plugin.js`'s actual source, not just this plan's earlier paraphrase of it.** The
table's "Yes (1 of 3)" for `product-detail/index.jsx:40` describes the **base** file's import —
but that file is shadowed by our own PDP override page and never loads. What actually matters is
*our own* `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx`'s import of `RecommendedProducts`, and
`isFromExtends` (`overrides-plugin.js:128-146`) returns **false** whenever the issuing file is
itself inside `overrides/` — its own doc comment says so plainly: *"This will return false if the
issuer is a file in the overrides dir."* Our PDP page's current package-path import
(`product-detail/index.tsx:59`) is therefore **not** redirected to our override, at all, regardless
of `Island`, scroll position, or Einstein data — none of which were ever the actual blocker.
Discovered live during A1's mandatory Cart/PDP verification (Marcel: zero marker fires on PDP even
after a full scroll to the bottom, while Cart fired correctly and repeatedly).

**Consequence, and why this isn't just a testing nuisance:** as originally planned, PDP's Recently
Viewed rail would never render even after A6 lands the branch — Cart would work, PDP would
silently not, and SFCC-83's PDP requirement would ship broken with no test catching it (no PR-time
E2E on this path either, per the Loop depth section below). **Fix, folded into A6 (Marcel,
2026-09-06):** change `product-detail/index.tsx:59`'s `RecommendedProducts` import from the base
package path to a relative path pointing at our own override, per
`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s existing "Importing an already-overridden component from a
new component" rule — the exact same doctrine
A6 already applies to `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` below, just missed for `RecommendedProducts` itself
in the original draft of this plan. See A6's updated step and pass criteria.

Two of those six are on **PLP**, explicitly descoped at adjudication #2. The override *loads* there
but its branch never fires (those rails use `EMPTY_SEARCH_RESULTS_*` recommenders), so **no Recently
Viewed rail appears on PLP**. State this in the PR body so a reviewer does not read the override's
presence on PLP as scope creep.

Rejected alternative — re-homing the fetch into a new Zimmermann container: still needs a per-surface
caller, and Cart is a base page we cannot pass props to without the 2,460-line port. Buys nothing,
costs the port.

### Branch: ONE, single PR (Marcel, 2026-09-06)

**`feature/SFCC-83-84_recently-viewed`**, cut from `feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component`.

An earlier draft proposed two stacked branches. **Marcel chose a single branch / single PR to
maintain**, which is now the plan. Step IDs keep their `A*`/`B*` prefixes (they read as "rail work"
and "page work") but execute as one sequence on one branch:

> A1 → A2 → A3 → A4 → A5 → A6 → B1 → B2 → B3 → GATES

**What this buys:**
- **The AC 5 / AC 84-1 split disappears.** Those two ACs are the *same* requirement. On two branches
  the rail would have shipped with an unsupplied `seeAllHref` and SFCC-83 could not be marked Done
  until the second PR merged. On one branch the link and its destination land together — no
  interim state where the link points at a 404, and both stories close on one merge.
- One review conversation, one CI run, one changelog entry.

**What it costs, stated plainly:**
- **The four-team CODEOWNERS fan-out on `overrides/app/routes.tsx` (`CODEOWNERS:94`) now applies to
  the whole PR**, not just the page half. Every reviewer group sees the full diff.
- **The provisional-design page now gates the confirmed-design rail.** SFCC-83's rail is authoritative
  at all three viewports and corroborated twice; SFCC-84's page comes entirely from a provisional
  source. If the page's design is challenged in review, the rail — which re-skins two live surfaces
  and has no such doubt — waits with it. Accepted deliberately; flag it in the PR body so a reviewer
  knows the rail can be split back out if the page stalls.

### Loop depth

Two stories, ~22 files, one 236-line copy-first file. Mid-size build.

- **Full implementer → tester → scorer** on A2, A3, A4, A5, B1, B3 — where a silent wrong answer
  ships (a variation flag misread from Figma; an ordering/cap bug of exactly the shape the FED
  handbook's finding 18 warns encodes itself into a passing test; an AC-8 gate that never fires).
- **Implementer + scorer only** on A1, A6, B2, A7, B4 — their gate is mechanical (`tsc`, `npm run
  test`, a diff read); a tester pass adds a round-trip without adding a check.

**Deliberately dropped, with reasons:**
- **No Playwright/E2E.** Adding an allow-list group to `.github/workflows/qa.yml` is Tier 1 CI config
  (`CODEOWNERS:65`) — out of scope. Without it these paths resolve to `e2e_scope: skip` and there is
  no PR-time E2E run either way (`.claude/rules/testing.md` > Change-scoped E2E). State this in both
  PR bodies rather than implying coverage exists.
- **No page-level Storybook story.** No page in this repo has one; the presentational organisms carry
  the stories, matching `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/partials/*.stories.tsx`.
- **No new `theme/components/*Shared.ts`.** Both recipes derive media queries from `breakpoints`
  imported from `app/theme/foundation` — one source, two importers, no copied literal.
- **No visual-regression tooling.** None exists; Figma parity is checked by eye against named nodes.

### PLP surface — 🟢 DECIDED 2026-09-08 (Marcel): fold into this single PR

**Superseded, not refined.** This plan's original scope line ("PLP is out; SFCC-83 AC 9 knowingly
not met") was written against `.docs/prd/search.md` §7.4's "PDP + Cart" framing and never checked
against the ticket's own AC text. Marcel supplied the full verbatim SFCC-83 ticket 2026-09-07; its
AC states plainly: *"Confirmed surfaces are PLP, PDP, and Cart."* PLP is real, in-scope, unbuilt
work, not a knowingly-deferred gap — the earlier "Routed, not planned into" note calling AC 9
wrong-as-written (bottom of this document) is itself the thing that was wrong, and is corrected
there.

**What's missing.** Unlike PDP and Cart, PLP has no existing base call site rendering a
`RecommendedProducts`-style rail keyed to `EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` /
`'viewed-recently-einstein'`. The two PLP-side consumers this plan's own architecture-fork table
already identified (`product-list/partials/empty-results.jsx`'s top-sellers/most-viewed rails) use
the `EMPTY_SEARCH_RESULTS_*` recommenders instead, and only render on an empty search — not the
general "you've been browsing" placement PLP needs. This means PLP needs a **new call site**, not a
branch inside an existing one — most likely a new `RecommendedProducts` usage added to
`overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` or a `product-list/partials/` file. That path is
**Squad A territory** per `.claude/rules/squadA.md` — a different owner than every other file this
plan touches (all Squad B / shared so far), and that rule file requires notifying the Squad A Lead
before touching it.

**Not designed yet.** No Figma node in either the original set or Marcel's 2026-09-07 supply is
confirmed as "Recently Viewed on PLP" specifically — the closest candidates are the unread
`Zimmermann_Designs` `9086:*` family (see Open Question 15, pending Figma auth). Placement (top of
grid? after N rows? sidebar?) is undetermined.

**Decided 2026-09-08 (Marcel): "we're doing PLP as well."** Folds into this single PR, not a
fast-follow. This does expand the file manifest into a fourth owner and a page tier this plan
hadn't touched (Squad A pages) — the "spans multiple protection tiers" condition AGENTS.md Hard
Rule #10 flags — but the decision itself is now made; add a real file-manifest row (below) and
notify the Squad A Lead per `squadA.md` before touching `product-list/`.

**Still genuinely open: exact placement.** No Figma node anywhere in the supplied set is confirmed
as "Recently Viewed on PLP" specifically — not designed yet, not guessed here. Mechanically, the
new call site is a `<RecommendedProducts recommender={EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED}
.../>` added to `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx` (or a `product-list/partials/` file,
if the eventual placement sits inside an existing partial rather than the page shell) — the same
mechanical pattern PDP/Cart already use, wired through the same interim data source as A6 (§2). The
open question is purely *where in the page* (top of grid? after N rows? sidebar?), not whether or
how it's wired. **Owner: Marcel — confirm placement before this specific file is written**, though
nothing else in this PR needs to wait on it.

### Interim data source — Einstein unavailable, ship against real browser-tracked history (Marcel, 2026-09-08)

**Why this exists.** Einstein is confirmed "Not Deployed" on every real Zimmermann site (see Open
Question 6) — not a data-quality nuance, a total absence of any engine to call. Rather than block
the whole build on a platform-provisioning timeline outside this team's control, Marcel directed:
ship the UI now against **real, live Commerce Cloud product data**, sourced by **this browser's own
actual view history**, tracked client-side — not Einstein, and not any hardcoded/mocked fixture
(AGENTS.md's "no mocking" rule is fully respected: every product shown is real and live-fetched,
only the *list of which IDs to fetch* is sourced differently). A follow-up ticket (not yet created)
swaps that one seam for real Einstein once SFCC-112 unblocks; everything else in this build is
intended to survive that swap unchanged.

**The seam, precisely — this is what makes the later swap small.** Two independent concerns, today
both interim, only one of which changes later:
1. **"Which product IDs has this shopper recently viewed?"** — today: read from browser storage,
   written by this shopper's own PDP visits. Later: Einstein's `getRecommendations` response. **This
   is the only piece the Einstein follow-up ticket touches.**
2. **"Given those IDs, fetch real product data and turn it into cards"** — a live Shopper Products
   `getProducts` call (`allImages: true`, `perPricebook: true`, `expand: [...]` — the same
   three-flag combination already confirmed correct three independent times this session: Einstein's
   own `fetchRecProductDetails`, the PLP quick-test mapper, and the `zimmproductcard-live-demo`
   branch) plus a mapper. **This is real, permanent work regardless of data source** — it's the same
   was/now-pricing (`getPriceData`) and multi-image (`imageGroups`) work B2 already needed (Open
   Question 16), not thrown away when Einstein arrives.

**What this revises (already-committed steps, not just new B1/B2 work):**
- **A4** — `useRecentlyViewedGate.ts` is renamed to `useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` and extended: it
  already writes a session flag on PDP view; it now also **records the viewed product's ID**, not
  just a boolean. Not a protected/shared hook (not on either hook-protection list, single consumer
  today), so the rename costs nothing structurally — see A4's rewrite below. This is the one file
  where "browser/local it is" is literally implemented.
- **A3** — the mapper's input shape changes from Einstein's merged rec+product object to a plain
  Shopper Product from our own `getProducts` call. Its output contract and its own scope decision
  (image-only, no price, no gallery — A2's `recentlyViewed` variation is unchanged) do **not**
  change; only where the input object comes from does.
- **A6** — the `recommender === EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED` branch trigger is
  unchanged (the base pages still pass that same recommender prop regardless of what we do with
  it) — what changes is that inside the branch, `recommendations.recs` (Einstein's response) is
  never read; the new history hook + a real `getProducts` call are used instead.
- **B2** — same swap: the page container calls the new history hook instead of
  `getRecommendations`, and feeds the stored ID list (**capped at 24, not the rail's 5-item
  slice** — see the stored-history-cap note below, superseded from an earlier "full, uncapped"
  framing once the `getProducts` 24-ID limit was discovered) into the richer was/now/multi-image
  mapper already planned.

**Storage mechanics, per "browser/local it is":**
- **Guests:** `sessionStorage` — unchanged from A4's existing design, still correctly satisfies AC 6
  (session-scoped, cleared at session end).
- **Registered shoppers:** `localStorage` — a genuine, explicit, temporary deviation from both AC 7
  ("available on login from any device") and the ticket's own Assumption ("storage... handled by
  SFCC"). `localStorage` survives closing the browser (better than nothing, testable), but is still
  **device-local** — it cannot and will not satisfy cross-device continuity. This is not a
  workaround for that AC, it's an explicit, stated non-fix pending the Einstein follow-up — must be
  called out plainly in the PR body and to whoever signs off testing, not discovered by a confused
  reviewer. AC 7 should be marked N/A-pending-follow-up for this PR, not silently tested against a
  single device and called passing.
- **De-duplication / ordering:** viewing a product already in history moves it to the front rather
  than creating a duplicate entry — required for AC 2's "most-recent-first" to hold up under repeat
  views, and needs its own explicit test (view A, B, A again → order must be `[A, B]`, not `[A, B, A]`
  or `[B, A]` misordered).
- **Stored-history cap — RESOLVED 2026-09-08, then SUPERSEDED same day once the 24-ID fetch limit
  was discovered.** Original reasoning (Marcel: "how would this be treated if Einstein were
  available? do the same as that"): real Einstein has no client-supplied "how far back to
  remember" parameter, so this isn't a product/UX decision — `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED =
  500` was set as a generous engineering safety ceiling against unbounded growth. **That reasoning
  is now incomplete, not wrong** — it was correct given what was known at the time, but didn't yet

### A4 — Recently-viewed history hook, plus the PDP write

**🔴 REVISED 2026-09-08 — renamed and re-designed, per "Interim data source" in §2. Read this whole
step before implementing; the original boolean logic below is no longer correct and would ship a
real bug if built as originally specced.**

Create `overrides/app/hooks/useRecentlyViewedHistory.ts` (was `useRecentlyViewedGate.ts`).

This still answers **finding 28** — the *original* concern was that Einstein's recommender returns a
two-product baseline for a visitor with zero history, so `recs.length === 0` never fires and AC 8
isn't implementable from the response. With Einstein out of the picture for this build, that specific
failure mode can't happen either way (there is no Einstein response to leak a baseline from) — but
the fix is still needed, now for a more basic reason: something has to track what "recently viewed"
even means without Einstein.

**The boolean logic changes, not just the storage mechanism — this is the one real gotcha in this
revision.** The original design was:

```
hasRecentlyViewed = sessionFlagIsSet || isRegistered
```

`isRegistered` was a deliberate short-circuit: trust that a logged-in shopper has *some* server-side
Einstein history even on a fresh device. **That assumption breaks entirely once Einstein is out of
the loop** — there is no server-side history to trust anymore. Built as originally specced, every
registered shopper would show `hasRecentlyViewed = true` unconditionally, including one who has
never viewed anything in this interim system on any device — gating the rail *open* with zero real
cards behind it. That's a real, shippable bug, not a hypothetical; it must not be carried into the
interim build. **Corrected logic:**

```
hasRecentlyViewed = recentlyViewedIds.length > 0
```

— true for both guests and registered shoppers alike, based purely on this interim system's own
tracked history. `isRegistered` still matters, just for a different purpose now: it selects *which*
storage to read/write (see below), not whether to bypass the check.

**New return shape:** `{hasRecentlyViewed: boolean, recentlyViewedIds: readonly string[],
markProductViewed: (productId: string) => void}` — the boolean is now derived from the ID list, not
tracked independently, so the two can never disagree.

- `markProductViewed(productId)` writes to `sessionStorage` (guest) or `localStorage` (registered,
  via `isRegistered` from `useCustomerType()` — the same hook `use-einstein.js:449` already uses) —
  called from the existing Einstein `useEffect` in
  `overrides/app/pages/product-detail/index.tsx` (lines 772–801), alongside the
  `einstein.sendViewProduct` calls already there (left untouched — that call is unrelated real
  analytics, not this build's concern). One import, one call, guarded by the same `if (product)`.
- **De-duplication / move-to-front:** if `productId` is already in the stored list, remove the old
  entry before prepending — never a duplicate, and a re-view correctly becomes "most recent" again.
- **Cap the stored list** at `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` (**24, superseded from an earlier
  500 same day — see §2** — matches the Full History page's own 24-ID fetch cap, since nothing
  beyond item 24 is ever displayable) — trim from the tail, oldest-first, on write.

**AC mapping, restated for the interim system:** `sessionStorage` is session-scoped and cleared at
session end — **AC 6**, unchanged. **AC 7 (cross-device for registered shoppers) is explicitly
*not* satisfied by this interim design** — `localStorage` is still device-local. This must be stated
plainly in the PR body and marked N/A-pending-the-Einstein-follow-up for this specific AC, not tested
against a single device and reported as passing. See §2's "Interim data source" for the full
reasoning — this is a stated, accepted gap, not an oversight.

**Confirmed 2026-09-07, not a frontend gap** (pre-dates and is unaffected by this revision — restated
for continuity): SFCC-83's own Assumptions section states *"the storage of Recently Viewed is
handled by SFCC."* The interim system above is a **temporary, explicit stand-in** for that
assumption while Einstein is unavailable, not a rejection of it — once the Einstein follow-up lands,
this hook's job reverts to a thin boolean/gate again and the real history moves back server-side, per
the original design intent this section used to describe.

**Superseded by the above, not applicable to the interim build:** the old "stated assumption" about
a registered shopper with genuinely zero Einstein history still seeing a two-product baseline
(Open Question 6's original framing) — that residual was specific to trusting Einstein's own
baseline behaviour, which the interim system never calls, so it cannot leak through here. It returns
once the Einstein follow-up is built, at which point Open Question 6's original text applies again.

**Pass criteria**
- SSR-safe: initial state `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: []}`, resolved in
  `useEffect`. No storage access during render. No hydration mismatch — the rail does not exist on
  first paint and appears after hydration. (Also good for LCP; the PDP rail is inside
  `<Island hydrateOn='visible'>` anyway.)
- Wrapped in `try/catch` — Safari private mode throws on both `sessionStorage` and `localStorage`.
  Failure degrades to `{hasRecentlyViewed: false, recentlyViewedIds: []}`, never an exception.
- JSDoc with `@returns` (`components.md` > Hooks).
- Vitest: empty storage + guest → `false`/`[]`; one ID + guest → `true`/`[id]`; empty storage +
  **registered** → `false`/`[]` (**the corrected case — must be tested explicitly, since this is
  exactly where the old short-circuit bug would have shipped silently**); re-viewing an existing ID
  moves it to front with no duplicate; writing past the cap trims the oldest entry; storage throwing
  → safe empty default; first render before effect → safe empty default.
- **Make each fail on purpose first.** The FED handbook's finding 18 trap is a test that passes
  because it was written against the only arrangement already correct — this applies doubly to the
  registered-with-zero-history case above, since that's precisely the case the old logic got wrong.
- The PDP change is exactly two lines (now passing `product.id` into `markProductViewed`, not a
  no-arg call). Nothing else in `product-detail/index.tsx` moves (AGENTS.md Hard Rule #5 — no
  refactoring upward).

### A5 — `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` organism + recipe

Create `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmRecentlyViewedRail/` (`index.tsx`,
`zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`, `index.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx`); register
`ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`.

**Purely presentational — data as props.** Props: `title: ReactNode`, `cards: readonly
ZimmProductCardProps[]`, `seeAllHref?: string`, `seeAllLabel?: string`. No `useEinstein`, no
`useIntl` — the container owns the copy. (An `IntlProvider` wrapper is still needed in the test
because `ZimmProductCard` itself calls `useIntl`; follow `zimmProductCard/index.test.tsx`'s wrapper.)

Structure mirrors Figma: a `title-and-link` row (title left, See-Full-History link right) above a
horizontally scrollable `group` of `ZimmProductCard`s at `variation: 'recentlyViewed'`.

**No rail-level arrow buttons.** Desktop `40000307:12444` decomposes into exactly two children —
`title-and-link` (1440×96) and `group` (1440×432) — with no arrow layer. `ZimmProductCard` already
carries its own intra-card arrows; rail arrows would collide. Native scroll with scroll-snap only.

**Three explicit media queries** off `breakpoints` imported from `app/theme/foundation`, never Chakra's
array shorthand (it fails `recipeGuards.test.ts`). Real geometry, read from the nodes 2026-09-06:

| Viewport | Rail node | Card | Cards across |
|---|---|---|---|
| Mobile (base, 402) | `40000538:25030` — 402×355.82 | **201×299.82** | **2** (201×2 = 402, exactly full-bleed) |
| Tablet (`breakpoints.md`, 768) | `40000730:13363` — 768×437.85 | **256×381.85** | **3** |
| Desktop (`breakpoints.xl`) | `40000307:12444` — 1440×528 | **288×432** | **5** |

All three cards are 2:3, matching `ZimmProductCardMedia`'s existing `aspectRatio: '2 / 3'` — so card
width is the only thing that varies per breakpoint; height follows. Header (`title-and-link`) is
**h96** on Desktop (`40000538:20306`) and **h56** on Mobile (`40000538:25031`); the link is present on
both, so it is never hidden by viewport.

## plugin:figma:figma
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

SKILLS (Prefer the skills shipped with the Figma plugin on the agent being used. If no Figma plugin is installed, use the skills served by the Figma MCP resource):
- /figma-use — MANDATORY before calling use_figma; fallback: skill://figma/figma-use/SKILL.md

  values).
- Order preserved verbatim (no ordering AC, but the page is the rail's overflow — same order or it
  reads as broken). Test with a distinguishable ordering.
- Item count renders from `cards.length` — **no separate count source.** Assert the displayed count
  equals the number of rendered tiles; a divergence is the bug this criterion exists to catch.
- Story titled `Commerce/ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`; exports `Default`, `SingleItem`, `ManyItems`.
- Header comment names the provisional node ids.

### B2 — Page container + route

Create `overrides/app/pages/recentlyViewed/index.tsx` — a thin container: reads `recentlyViewedIds`
off A4's `useRecentlyViewedHistory()` (**🔴 REVISED 2026-09-08** — was `useEinstein().
getRecommendations(EINSTEIN_RECOMMENDERS.PDP_RECENTLY_VIEWED)`, per "Interim data source" in §2;
`getRecommendations` is not called at all by this page in the interim build), fetches real product
data for the stored ID list via `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` — **capped at 24, not the rail's
5-item slice** (was described as "full, uncapped" before the `getProducts` 24-ID-per-request limit
was discovered during Phase 1; the storage layer itself is now also capped at 24 for the same
reason, so this page genuinely does receive its full available history, just one that's bounded
by design rather than literally unbounded) — maps through **a new mapper (see
below — not A3's)**, renders `ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid`, owns the `react-intl` copy, and sets
`getTemplateName = () => 'recently-viewed'` per the four existing page precedents. Add
`RECENTLY_VIEWED_ROUTE = '/recently-viewed'` to `overrides/app/constants/index.ts`. Add the route to
`routes.tsx`.

**🔴 REVISED 2026-09-07 — "maps through A3's mapper" was wrong; a new mapper is needed, but no new
data-fetching architecture is.** Jasmijn's newest SFCC-84 comment specifies the Full History card's
default state as *"image, name, badge, price (incl. was/now), and cart icon"* — i.e. exactly the
`plp` variation's existing, already-shipped shape (B1's hover-behaviour cross-check above confirms
the rest). **A3's mapper cannot feed this**: by its own docblock it deliberately returns only
`{id, href, name, primaryImage, currentPrice}` — no `originalPrice`, no `images` — because A2/A3 were
scoped for the rail's image-only design, not the page's full card.

**Still fully valid after the 2026-09-08 data-source swap above — restated, not re-derived.** This
finding was originally verified against Einstein's `fetchRecProductDetails`, which internally calls
`getProducts` with `allImages: true` / `perPricebook: true` / `expand: [...]`. The interim
`recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` calls the **same underlying Shopper Products endpoint with the same
flags** (see §2) — just triggered by our own tracked ID list instead of Einstein's rec list — so
every field this finding relies on (`imageGroups`, `tieredPrices`) is equally present either way. The
was/now-pricing and multi-image work below was never actually Einstein-specific; it was already
correct once the underlying `getProducts` call is right, regardless of who supplies the ID list.

**Verified 2026-09-07 (pre-dates the interim-source revision; kept as the technical record), directly
against source, not assumed:** the data those extra fields need is already flowing through the
*same* underlying Shopper Products call both A3's original Einstein-sourced design and this page
consume. `use-einstein.js`'s `fetchRecProductDetails`
(`node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/hooks/use-einstein.js:465-505`) does a real Shopper
Products `getProducts` call — `allImages: true`, `perPricebook: true`, `expand: ['prices',
'promotions', 'images', 'variations', ...]` — and merges the full result as `{...rec, ...product,
productId, image: {...}}`. So the object any mapper here receives already carries
`product.imageGroups` (real multi-image galleries — the same field
`productListCardMapper.ts`'s own `selectGalleryImages` already reads off a Search hit) and
`product.tieredPrices` (per-pricebook pricing). Base SFCC ships a ready-made utility for exactly
this shape — `getPriceData` (`app/utils/product-utils.js:123`) — which already derives `listPrice`
(the max of `tieredPrices`, i.e. "was"), the current tiered `price` ("now"), and `isOnSale =
currentPrice < listPrice`. **Neither A3 nor `productListCardMapper.ts` calls it; both explicitly set
`originalPrice: undefined` instead, with comments claiming the data or the logic isn't available.**
That claim is now known to be inaccurate for the Einstein pipeline specifically — raised as Open
Question 16 rather than silently rewritten into A3, since A3 is already-committed, scored work and
changing its behaviour now is a distinct decision from documenting this plan correctly.

**Consequence (restated 2026-09-08 for the interim source, same conclusion either way):** no
*second* product-detail fetch is needed on top of the one `recentlyViewedProductFetch.ts` already
makes (originally written as "on top of what `getRecommendations`/`fetchRecProductDetails` already
does," back when Einstein was still the assumed source — the underlying point is unchanged: one
`getProducts`-shaped call, correctly flagged, already carries everything needed). What's needed is a
**new mapper**, `overrides/app/utils/recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` (added to the file manifest),
that:
- calls base `getPriceData(product)` and maps `listPrice`/`price` to `originalPrice`/`currentPrice`,
  only setting `originalPrice` when `isOnSale` is true — a not-on-sale product should not render a
  crossed-out price identical to its current one;
- reuses (or ports, if `productListCardMapper.ts`'s own types don't line up — decide at
  implementation time) `selectGalleryImages`'s image-group-picking logic against
  `product.imageGroups`;
- produces `variation: 'plp'`-shaped props (badge, size chips, hover-swap image), not A3's narrow
  `recentlyViewed` shape.

**Honest caveat, not provable from code alone:** whether `tieredPrices` actually comes back with
more than one entry depends on Zimmermann's live SFCC pricebook configuration — with only one active
pricebook, `getPriceData` will correctly compute `isOnSale: false` every time (correct behaviour,
not a bug), but this can't be fully confirmed working until checked against a real on-sale product
in a running environment — same "verify in the running app" discipline as A1/A6/B3 elsewhere in
this plan.

**Empty state (DECIDED 2026-09-06 — from codebase precedent, not invented).** SFCC-84 has no
empty-state AC, and the house pattern never renders nothing: `EmptyCart`, `EmptySearchResults` and
`empty-wishlist` all render heading + copy + CTA. `EmptyCart` is the near-exact analogue (a personal
page that can legitimately be empty) and branches its copy on `isRegistered` — **the same value A4's
gate hook already computes**.

**Copy DECIDED 2026-09-08 (Marcel: "look for a pattern in the existing codebase and build off
that")** — read `EmptyCart` directly

  '--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-focused': colors.action.primary.bgFocused,
  '--zimm-color-action-primary-text': colors.action.primary.text,
  '--zimm-color-action-primary-text-disabled': colors.action.primary.textDisabled,

  // ---- Alias / Semantic: Action: Secondary ----
  '--zimm-color-action-secondary-border': colors.action.secondary.border,
  '--zimm-color-action-secondary-bg-hover': colors.action.secondary.bgHover,
  '--zimm-color-action-secondary-text': colors.action.secondary.text,
  '--zimm-color-action-secondary-text-inverse': colors.action.secondary.textInverse,
  '--zimm-color-action-secondary-text-disabled': colors.action.secondary.textDisabled,

  // ---- Typography: Font families ----
  // Both heading and body resolve to the same stack, headed by Futura Round.
  // Sourced from ./fonts so the CSS-variable surface and theme.fonts cannot drift
  // apart: text styled by a .zimm-* class and text styled by a Chakra prop must
  // fall back to the same face when Futura Round is unavailable. This intentionally
  // carries the richer fallback stack rather than the Handover's bare
  // "'Futura Round', sans-serif" — see the rationale in ./fonts.ts.

  '--zimm-font-family-body': FONT_REGULAR,
  '--zimm-font-family-serif': FONT_SERIF,

  // ---- Typography: Font sizes ----
  '--zimm-font-size-md': fontSizes.md,
  '--zimm-font-size-xs': fontSizes.xs,
  '--zimm-font-size-2xs': fontSizes['2xs'],
  '--zimm-font-size-3xs': fontSizes['3xs'],
  '--zimm-font-size-4xs': fontSizes['4xs'],

  // ---- Typography: Line heights ----
  '--zimm-font-lineheight-md': lineHeights.md,
  '--zimm-font-lineheight-xs': lineHeights.xs,
  '--zimm-font-lineheight-2xs': lineHeights['2xs'],
  '--zimm-font-lineheight-3xs': lineHeights['3xs'],
  '--zimm-font-lineheight-4xs': lineHeights['4xs'],

  // ---- Typography: Letter spacing ----
  '--zimm-font-letterspacing-sm': letterSpacings.sm,
  '--zimm-font-letterspacing-xs': letterSpacings.xs,
  '--zimm-font-letterspacing-2xs': letterSpacings['2xs'], // -0.14px — see typography.ts
  '--zimm-font-letterspacing-footer': letterSpacings.footer,

  // ---- Typography: Font weights ----
  '--zimm-font-weight-medium': fontWeights.medium,
  '--zimm-font-weight-regular': fontWeights.regular,

  // ---- Spacing scale (named) ----
  '--zimm-scale-3xs': spacing['3xs'],
  '--zimm-scale-2xs': spacing['2xs'],
  '--zimm-scale-xs': spacing.xs,
  '--zimm-scale-s': spacing.s,
  '--zimm-scale-m': spacing.m,
  '--zimm-scale-l': spacing.l,
  '--zimm-scale-xl': spacing.xl,
  '--zimm-scale-2xl': spacing['2xl'],
  '--zimm-scale-3xl': spacing['3xl'],
  '--zimm-scale-4xl': spacing['4xl'],
  '--zimm-scale-5xl': spacing['5xl'],
  '--zimm-scale-6xl': spacing['6xl'],
  '--zimm-scale-7xl': spacing['7xl'],

  // ---- Spacing: numeric aliases ----
  // Ported from the Handover's numeric spacing scale. The ones below that coincide
  // with a named-scale step reference it directly; the rest have no foundation-file
  // source to derive from (not duplicates — genuinely distinct Handover values), so
  // they stay as literals.
  '--zimm-scale-025': '1px',
  '--zimm-scale-200': spacing.xs, // 8px
  '--zimm-scale-300': spacing.s, // 12px
  '--zimm-scale-400': spacing.m, // 16px
  '--zimm-scale-500': spacing.l, // 20px
  '--zimm-scale-600': spacing.xl, // 24px
  '--zimm-scale-700': '28px',
  '--zimm-scale-800': spacing['2xl'], // 32px
  '--zimm-scale-1000': spacing['3xl'], // 40px
  '--zimm-scale-1100': '44px',
  '--zimm-scale-1200': '48px',
  '--zimm-scale-1300': '52px',
  '--zimm-scale-1600': spacing['4xl'], // 64px
  '--zimm-scale-3500': '140px',
  '--zimm-scale-4500': '180px',

  // ---- Spacing: Grid margins ----
  '--zimm-grid-margin-mobile': grid.containerPadding.base,
  '--zimm-grid-margin-tablet': grid.containerPadding.md,
  '--zimm-grid-margin-desktop': grid.containerPadding.xl || '0px',
  // Outer container cap — shared by header/footer/main content. 'none' today; see

  '--zimm-grid-max-width': grid.maxWidth,

  '--zimm-size-action-height-lg': actionSizes.height.lg,
  '--zimm-size-action-height-md': actionSizes.height.md,
  '--zimm-size-action-padding-h-lg': actionSizes.paddingX.lg,
  '--zimm-size-action-padding-h-md': actionSizes.paddingX.md,
  '--zimm-size-action-gap': actionSizes.gap,

  // ---- Border widths ----
  '--zimm-border-width-default': borderWidths.default,

  // ---- Icon sizes ----
  '--zimm-icon-size-xl': iconSizes.xl,
  '--zimm-icon-size-lg': iconSizes.lg,
  '--zimm-icon-size-md': iconSizes.md,
  '--zimm-icon-size-sm': iconSizes.sm,

  // ---- Mega menu sizing ----
  '--zimm-size-mega-menu-two-column-max-width': megaMenuSizes.twoColumnMaxWidth,

  // ---- Motion (PROVISIONAL — pending formal sign-off, see motion.ts) ----
  '--zimm-motion-duration-fast': motion.duration.fast,
  '--zimm-motion-duration-default': motion.duration.default,
  '--zimm-motion-duration-slow': motion.duration.slow,
  '--zimm-motion-easing-standard': motion.easing.standard,
  '--zimm-motion-easing-slides': motion.easing.slides,
  '--zimm-motion-easing-fades': motion.easing.fades,
};

Figma's own Home node still shows * the Tag layer un-hidden, contradicting that scope note — treating the confirmed written * requirement as authoritative over the file's possibly-stale layer visibility here, flagged * rather than silently picked. * * Badge count (confirmed after the above shipped, via a Dev Mode Connect Note on the separate * "Product Cards" Figma file — QQ427wHWEUjsjP7H8v48Rs, node 3448:35976 — distinct from the * design-system component-set file cited throughout this docblock): "only 1 product badge will * show up on these product cards - depending on the configured hierarchy, the highest priority * badge will be shown," with that priority logic owned by SFCC-225. This confirms `badge?: * string` (a single value, not a list) is the correct, final shape for this prop — not a * placeholder pending a possible future move to an array. Treated the comment as more authoritative than the AC text here too: * `VARIATION_CONFIG.showHoverImageSwap` now suppresses the swap for `home` specifically. This * is unrelated to, and does not affect, Home's own * `hoverRevealsPrice` — that is a separate mechanism (a style flag consumed by this organism's * own recipe), not `swapOnHover`. * * Correction (SFCC-83, 2026-09-08): the paragraph above frames this as choosing Dani's comment * over a still-conflicting AC at ship time — that's not accurate. Jasmijn's 2026-08-17 AC edit * (see the changelog) removed the unconditional-core-hover-swap language before this shipped, * aligning the AC with Dani's note rather than leaving the two in conflict. Implementing per * Dani's note therefore also means implementing per the (already-corrected) AC — this was never * really an override of a live disagreement, just following the AC as it stood by the time this * was written. The shipped behaviour (`showHoverImageSwap: false` for `home`) is unaffected; only * this paragraph's framing of why was wrong. * * RESOLVED (SFCC-83, 2026-09-07): both quotes above, from Dani's scope note (Jira comment 13880 * on SFCC-236), truncate at the same point. import React from 'react';
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import { chakra, useMultiStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';
import { ZimmProductCard } from '../zimmProductCard';
import type { ZimmProductCardProps } from '../zimmProductCard';

export type ZimmRecentlyViewedGridProps = {
  /**
   * Typed as `ReactNode`, not `string` — this component owns no copy/intl, the same discipline
   * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `title` prop documents for itself (build plan §A5/§B1). Styled
   * with `textStyle="heading3"` directly below, applied from the start rather than left for a
   * caller to pre-style — the rail's own `title` shipped once *without* this and had to be fixed
   * after live Storybook testing caught it rendering in the ambient body weight instead of the
   * intended one (see `zimmRecentlyViewedRail/index.tsx`'s own docblock, "Styling resolved
   * 2026-09-08"). That token is independently confirmed correct for THIS component's own title
   * bar too, not just carried over from the rail: build plan §B1's `get_variable_defs` read on
   * Figma node `3332:37131` ("PLP Bar desktop") returns "Default/Heading 3" — Futura Round
   * Medium, size 16 / line-height 18 / letterSpacing -1 — cross-checked against
   * `theme/foundation/typography.ts`'s own registered `heading3` (`fontSizes.xs` 16px /
   * `lineHeights['2xs']` 18px / `letterSpacings.xs` -0.12px, the same documented sub-pixel
   * rounding `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s Units section already carries elsewhere /
   * `textTransform: uppercase` already baked in) and found to match exactly.
   */
  title: ReactNode;
  /**
   * A pre-formatted, already-pluralized node (e.g. "16 Items" / "1 Item") — this component does
   * not own copy/intl, matching `title` above and `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own container/
   * presentational split (`.claude/rules/components.md`). Build plan §B1: the item count is
   * mechanical ICU-plural-selector copy ("go for it" — Marcel, 2026-09-08), which is the calling
   * container's job (SFCC-84's Full History page container, not built by this step), not this
   * organism's. **Rendered exactly as received — never recomputed from `cards.length` here.** A
   * caller is expected to derive this from the same `cards` array it passes below; see this
   * component's own stories/tests for the "the two stay in sync when a real caller wires them
   * together correctly" proof this step's brief asked for — that proof lives at the call site
   * (story/test), not as internal recomputation, precisely so a future divergence between what a
   * caller *says* the count is and what actually rendered stays visible instead of being silently
   * papered over by this component re-deriving its own "correct" answer.
   *
   * Same `textStyle="heading3"` / colour treatment as `title` above — confirmed via the same
   * `3332:37131` screenshot, which renders "RECENTLY VIEWED" (left) and "16 ITEMS" (right) in the
   * same text style.
   */
  itemCountLabel: ReactNode;
  /**
   * Rendered in the exact order received — no sorting or reordering happens here, and (unlike
   * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`) no cap/slice either: SFCC-84's Full History page has no ordering AC
   * of its own, but per build plan §B1 "the page is the rail's overflow — same order or it reads
   * as broken", and the page container (not this component) is already responsible for capping
   * its fetch at `RECENTLY_VIEWED_HISTORY_MAX_STORED` (24, `app/constants/index.ts`) before this
   * component ever sees `cards` — see the build plan's B2 step. Typed as the full
   * `ZimmProductCardProps` union, matching `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own contract verbatim
   * (build plan §A5) rather than a variation-narrowed type, so this component spreads each entry
   * straight into `ZimmProductCard` rather than forcing a variation onto every card itself. In
   * real usage every entry already carries `variation: 'plp'` by construction — SFCC-84 AC 2 /
   * SFCC-236's own "Recently Viewed Full History variation (same behavior as PLP card)" AC block,
   * corroborated 2026-09-07/08 against the `feature/zimmproductcard-live-demo` branch's own
   * "Recently Viewed (Full History)" section, which renders `variation: 'plp'` cards with zero
   * different props from its own PLP demo cards (see this component's own recipe file for the
   * full citation). Nothing new was needed on `ZimmProductCard` itself for this — see that
   * component's own module docblock: *"'Recently Viewed Full History' is not a fourth
   * variation... callers pass `variation: 'plp'` for it."*
   */
  cards: readonly ZimmProductCardProps[];
};

const ZIMM_RECENTLY_VIEWED_GRID_RECIPE = 'ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid';

/**
 * SFCC-84 — the Recently Viewed Full History grid organism (build plan section B1). Purely
 * presentational: data arrives as props, no data-fetching, no `useEinstein`, no `useIntl` — the
 * same container/presentational split `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` (SFCC-83, build plan §A5) already
 * establishes, adapted here from a horizontally-scrolling rail to a 4-up desktop grid. The
 * container (build plan §B2, not built by this step) is responsible for reading the shopper's
 * tracked view history, fetching real product data for it, mapping the result to `plp`-shaped
 * `ZimmProductCardProps` (a new mapper, `recentlyViewedFullHistoryCard.ts` — NOT
 * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `recentlyViewedCard.ts`, whose narrower image-only output cannot
 * feed this grid's fuller `plp` card), and supplying `title`/`itemCountLabel` copy.
 *
 * **Design source, stated plainly per build plan §B1: this grid's layout comes from a
 * PROVISIONAL design source** (`Zimmermann_Designs` file, node `3332:35655` — not a PDP/Recently
 * Viewed node in the authoritative `Zimmermann_Design_System_2026` file the rail sibling uses;
 * see Marcel's 2026-09-04 precedence rule, restated verbatim in the build plan). That ranking is
 * unchanged by anything below. What DID change, this session (2026-09-07/08): the specific
 * geometry/typography/variation values actually used here were independently verified, not taken
 * on the provisional source's word alone —
 *   - **Layout** confirmed via live Figma metadata AND a real screenshot of `3332:37131` ("PLP
 *     Bar desktop", 1440×75), which renders "RECENTLY VIEWED" (left) / "16 ITEMS" (right) —
 *     confirming both the title-left/count-right layout and the title bar's own content in one
 *     node, not inferred from layer names alone (which the build plan notes were misleading here).
 *   - **The `Sidebar` (`3332:35664`) child holds four stacked `Products Module Desktop` instances**
 *     (`35665`/`35666`/`35668`/`35669`, each 1440×606) — two of which were checked directly and are
 *     structurally identical (four `Products S Desktop` instances each, 288×542, at
 *     x=0/384/768/1152): confirmed as 4 repeated example rows of real content, not 4 different
 *     states to design against.
 *   - **The `variation: 'plp'` decision** (see `cards`' own JSDoc above) is independently
 *     corroborated by a real, interactive prior-art branch, not just an AC-text reading — see this
 *     recipe file's own docblock for the full citation.
 *   - **The 96px horizontal card gap** (this recipe's own `GRID_CARD_GAP`) was checked at two
 *     independent Figma sources specifically because it does NOT resolve to any bound variable —
 *     see this recipe's own docblock for the full "RESOLVED... checked twice, genuinely
 *     un-tokenised" citation.
 * So: provisional design *source*, independently confirmed design *values* — both things are true
 * at once, and this docblock states both rather than letting the provisional-source caveat imply
 * the specific numbers below are unverified guesses, or letting the confirmed-values framing imply
 * the source ranking has changed.
 *
 * **This grid does NOT share its title row with `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail`'s own `title-and-link`**
 * (a deliberate build-plan call, not an oversight): the rail's header is Figma node
 * `40000538:20306` (h96/h56); this grid's is `3332:37131` (h75, one Desktop reading only, no
 * separate Tablet/Mobile node). Different components in Figma, so sharing would be a wrong DRY
 * call — see this recipe's own docblock for why no fixed header height is set here at all (unlike
 * the rail's own two-tier `HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE`/`DESKTOP`).
 *
 * Renders `null` for an empty `cards` array — the same defensive-leaf-component default
 * `ZimmRecentlyViewedRail` uses (its own container owns the actual "should this exist at all"
 * decision; SFCC-84's Full History page has its own separate empty-state design, per build plan
 * §B2, which does not involve mounting this component with zero cards at all).
 */
export const ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid = ({ title, itemCountLabel, cards }: ZimmRecentlyViewedGridProps) => {
  const styles = useMultiStyleConfig(ZIMM_RECENTLY_VIEWED_GRID_RECIPE, {});

  if (cards.length === 0) {
    return null;
  }

  return (
    <chakra.div __css={styles.container} data-testid="recently-viewed-grid">
      <chakra.div __css={styles.header}>
        <chakra.span textStyle="heading3" color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)">
          {title}
        </chakra.span>
        <chakra.span
          textStyle="heading3"
          color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)"
          data-testid="recently-viewed-grid-count"
        >
          {itemCountLabel}
        </chakra.span>
      </chakra.div>

        {cards.map((card) => (

 * the viewport exactly. This is a real grid, not a scroller — `grid` below uses fractional
 * (`1fr`) column tracks instead, so each card's rendered width falls out of the container width
 * divided across the current column count with nothing extra to style per card; `ZimmProductCard`
 * itself still has no width/height opinion of its own (`zimmProductCard.css.ts`), same precedent
 * the rail's own docblock already establishes.

 * Figma sources per Marcel's own steer (build plan §B1, "RESOLVED 2026-09-08, checked twice"): the
 * page-level instance (`3332:35655`) and, separately, the master "Product Card Group" component
 * (`40000301:11694`, `Size=Desktop, Display=4`, node `40000307:12446`) — both give identical
 * geometry (x 0/384/768/1152, 288px cards → 96px gaps, zero edge padding at the group's own frame
 * boundary). `get_variable_defs` at both scopes surfaces real spacing variables
 * (`alias/space/100` through `alias/space/2000`, i.e. 4 through 80px, plus 160/180) but none equal
 * 96. Independently re-checked here directly against this repo's own registered scale
 * (`foundation/spacing.ts`, read in full, not assumed from a comment): the named scale's own
 * nearest neighbours are `5xl` = 80px and `6xl` = 128px, and the numeric-alias scale
 * (`zimmTokens.ts`) jumps straight from `--zimm-scale-1600` (64px) to `--zimm-scale-3500` (140px)
 * — nothing at 96 on either scale. Treated exactly like `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`'s own
 * `CARD_WIDTH_MOBILE`/`TABLET`/`DESKTOP` precedent: a named constant carrying an explicit
 * pending-token comment, per `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s "Never" note — not a hardcoded
 * literal in the ordinary sense that rule targets. Expressed in rem, matching that same precedent
 * (a sizing/spacing dimension that should scale with root font-size/zoom, WCAG 1.4.4 — see
 * `overrideStyling.md`'s Units section).

 * `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`, which has a Mobile AND a Tablet AND a Desktop node) is the
 * Desktop one cited above — no Tablet/Mobile-specific card size or column count exists anywhere
 * in the provisional source for THIS grid. Per `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s "don't guess

 *     already-established "2-up on the smallest breakpoint" convention for a real product-card
 *     grid elsewhere in this exact codebase: `overrides/app/pages/product-list/index.tsx`'s own
 *     search-results `SimpleGrid columns={[2, 2, 4, 5]}` — a different page, different card width

 *   - Flagged here for confirmation once this grid sits inside a real page (build plan §B2),

 *     horizontal inset: getting the sub-desktop count wrong shows up as a real-world layout
 *     decision to revisit once a genuine Tablet/Mobile node exists, not a test failure — this
 *     organism has no assigned page context of its own.
 *

 * `HEADER_HEIGHT_MOBILE`/`DESKTOP`). The one Figma reading available (`3332:37131`, 75px,

 * "leave it simple, comment why" instruction this docblock's COLUMN COUNT section above follows
 * for the same underlying reason (one Desktop-only reading, no Tablet/Mobile counterpart).
 *
 * TITLE ROW HORIZONTAL INSET — also deliberately zero, for the same reason
 * `zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts`'s own `header` part gives its own title-and-link row: no

const GRID_CARD_GAP = '6rem'; // 96px — confirmed Figma value, checked at two independent sources (40000301:11694 "Product Card Group" master, Size=Desktop/Display=4, node 40000307:12446; and the page-level instance 3332:35655). No --zimm-scale-* equivalent (nearest neighbours: named scale 5xl=80px / 6xl=128px; numeric alias 1600=64px jumps straight to 3500=140px) — pending promotion to foundation/spacing.ts or sizes.ts by the UI designer.

// Column counts per breakpoint — see this file's own "COLUMN COUNT PER BREAKPOINT" docblock
// section above for the full reasoning (only Desktop is a confirmed Figma reading; the sub-desktop
// tier is a stated, flagged placeholder, not a guess presented as fact).
const GRID_COLUMNS_BASE = 2; // Mobile + Tablet (below breakpoints.xl) — UNCONFIRMED placeholder, see docblock.
const GRID_COLUMNS_DESKTOP = 4; // breakpoints.xl and up — confirmed (Figma nodes cited in the docblock above).

const DESKTOP_UP_QUERY = `@media (min-width: ${breakpoints.xl})`; // 1280px — same "Desktop" tier convention as zimmRecentlyViewedRail.css.ts's identically-named constant; the confirmed 4-up/288px reading itself comes from a 1440px Figma frame, inside this tier.

export const ZimmRecentlyViewedGrid = {
  parts: ['container', 'header', 'grid'],

  baseStyle: (): Record<string, SystemStyleObject> => ({
    container: {
      width: '100%',
    },

    header: {
      display: 'flex',
      alignItems: 'center',
      justifyContent: 'space-between',
    },

    grid: {
      display: 'grid',
      width: '100%',
      gridTemplateColumns: `repeat(${GRID_COLUMNS_BASE}, 1fr)`,
      columnGap: GRID_CARD_GAP,
      // Real registered token, referenced directly — see this file's own "VERTICAL (ROW) GAP"
      // docblock section above for why this one is NOT a named constant, unlike GRID_CARD_GAP.
      rowGap: 'var(--zimm-scale-1600)', // 64px
      [DESKTOP_UP_QUERY]: {
        gridTemplateColumns: `repeat(${GRID_COLUMNS_DESKTOP}, 1fr)`,
      },
    },
  }),
};
